thread.title: Apple Stock Hounded By iPhone Production Cuts | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Hounded By iPhone Production Cuts | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The steady drumbeat of negative reports about iPhone demand and production cuts continues to hound Apple stock. The news also has weighed on chip stocks with exposure to Apple 's ( AAPL ) iPhone business.
X The Wall Street Journal reported Monday that Apple has slashed production orders for all three of the iPhone models it unveiled in September. The report said Apple has cut production orders for the iPhone XR twice since late October.
Apple stock sank 4% to 185.86 on the stock market today . Since it gave disappointing guidance on Nov. 1, Apple stock has fallen 16.4% through Monday's close. The stock has traded below its 200-day moving average line for the last five sessions.
In a note to clients Sunday, RBC Capital Markets analyst Amit Daryanani said the Apple stock sell-off is "overdone."

Please contact customer service CLOSE IPhone Production Cuts Normal, But Earlier This Year "We haven't gone through a single iPhone cycle where there hasn't been 'noise' around supply-chain cuts," he said. However, he conceded that the cuts came earlier this cycle. Usually they happen after Thanksgiving, he said.
"We see high probability that Apple's guide for the December quarter factored in the recent negative production cuts and supply-chain pre-announcements," he said.
Daryanani reiterated his outperform rating on Apple stock with a price target of 240.
Chip Stocks Impacted By iPhone Production Cuts Meanwhile, several chip stocks have been knocked down by the iPhone production cuts. Among the chipmakers getting hit recently include Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ) and Qorvo ( QRVO ).
In a report Sunday, Cowen analyst Karl Ackerman said memory-chip makers are less impacted by iPhone cuts than radio-frequency chipmakers.
Over the past 12 months, the iPhone represented about 10% of all Nand chip demand and about 5% of DRAM demand, he said.
Reports from the supply chain indicate a reduction in iPhone production of 20 million units across the fourth quarter and first quarter, he said.
Micron Technology ( MU ) could see a reduction of 10 cents in earnings per share over the December and March quarters from lower iPhone memory chip sales. Western Digital ( WDC ) could see an impact of 15 cents in earnings per share over the two quarters, Ackerman said.
